189	/**
190	 * Initialize a profile directory: manifest, empty user patch layer, and the
191	 * pnpm settings out-of-tree plugins need. Existing files are never touched,
192	 * so re-running is a no-op on an initialized profile.
193	 * @param dir - the profile directory from {@link resolveProfileDir}.
194	 * @param bundles - the initial `dsh.profile.bundles` layer list.
195	 * @param patchReload - user patch-file lifecycle; custom profiles default to live reload.
196	 */
197	export function initProfile(
198	  dir: string,
199	  bundles: readonly string[],
200	  patchReload: ProfilePatchReload = DEFAULT_PROFILE_PATCH_RELOAD,
201	): void {
202	  mkdirSync(dir, { recursive: true })
203	  const manifestPath = join(dir, 'package.json')
204	  if (!existsSync(manifestPath)) {
205	    const manifest: ProfileManifest & { private: boolean } = {
206	      name: `dsh-profile-${basename(dir)}`,
207	      private: true,
208	      dependencies: {},
209	      dsh: { profile: { bundles: [...bundles], patchReload } },
210	    }
211	    writeFileSync(manifestPath, JSON.stringify(manifest, undefined, 2) + '\n')
212	  }
213	  const patchPath = join(dir, PROFILE_PATCH_FILENAME)
214	  if (!existsSync(patchPath)) writeFileSync(patchPath, PROFILE_PATCH_TEMPLATE)
215	  const workspacePath = join(dir, 'pnpm-workspace.yaml')
216	  if (!existsSync(workspacePath)) writeFileSync(workspacePath, PROFILE_PNPM_WORKSPACE)
217	}
218	
219	function readModuleProxyRecord(link: string): ModuleProxyRecord | undefined {
220	  try {
221	    return JSON.parse(readFileSync(join(link, 'package.json'), 'utf8')) as ModuleProxyRecord
222	  } catch {
223	    // Missing or invalid metadata is not managed state; callers reject it.
224	    return undefined
225	  }
226	}
227	
228	/** Ensure `link` is a symlink to `target`, replacing a wrong link or a dsh-managed packaged proxy. */
229	function ensureSymlink(link: string, target: string): void {
230	  let stat
231	  try {
232	    stat = lstatSync(link)
233	  } catch {
234	    // Missing link (first run) — created below. Any other lstat failure on a
235	    // path we just created the parent of would resurface on symlinkSync.
236	    stat = undefined
237	  }
238	  if (stat !== undefined) {
239	    if (!stat.isSymbolicLink()) {
240	      const existing = stat.isDirectory() ? readModuleProxyRecord(link) : undefined
241	      if (existing?.dsh?.moduleFallback?.targets === undefined) {
242	        throw new Error(`dsh: ${link} exists and is not a symlink or dsh-managed module proxy; remove it so dsh can manage the installation fallback`)
243	      }
244	      rmSync(link, { recursive: true })
245	      stat = undefined
246	    }
247	    if (stat !== undefined) {
248	      if (symlinkPointsTo(link, target)) return
249	      // unlink deletes the reparse point itself on Windows too; rmSync treats a
250	      // junction as a directory and throws EISDIR unless recursive.
251	      unlinkSync(link)
252	    }
253	  }
254	  try {
255	    symlinkSync(target, link, 'junction')
256	  } catch (error) {
257	    // Concurrent launches heal the same fallback; losing the race to a
258	    // process writing the identical link is success, anything else is not.
259	    // The window between the lstat miss above and this write cannot be
260	    // staged deterministically from the public API.
261	    /* v8 ignore next 4 */
262	    if ((error as NodeJS.ErrnoException).code !== 'EEXIST'
263	      || !lstatSync(link).isSymbolicLink() || !symlinkPointsTo(link, target)) {
264	      throw error
265	    }
266	  }
267	}
268	
269	/** Resolve a link target without following the final path component. */
270	function canonicalLinkPath(path: string): string | undefined {
271	  try {
272	    return join(realpathSync.native(dirname(path)), basename(path))
273	  } catch (error) {
274	    // A missing parent means the candidate cannot identify an existing owned link.
275	    /* v8 ignore next 2 -- a non-ENOENT realpath failure requires a host filesystem fault */
276	    if ((error as NodeJS.ErrnoException).code === 'ENOENT') return undefined
277	    /* v8 ignore next -- see the host-filesystem exception above */
278	    throw error
279	  }
280	}
281	
282	/** Return whether a symlink or junction points at the same path as `target`. */
283	function symlinkPointsTo(link: string, target: string): boolean {
284	  const actual = resolve(dirname(link), readlinkSync(link))
285	  const canonicalActual = canonicalLinkPath(actual)
286	  const canonicalTarget = canonicalLinkPath(resolve(target))
287	  return canonicalActual !== undefined && canonicalActual === canonicalTarget
288	}
289	
290	/** Add one profile-owned fallback link without replacing a pnpm-managed entry. */
291	function ensureProfileSymlink(link: string, target: string): void {
292	  try {
293	    lstatSync(link)
294	    return
295	  } catch (error) {
296	    /* v8 ignore next -- a non-ENOENT lstat failure requires a host filesystem fault */
297	    if ((error as NodeJS.ErrnoException).code !== 'ENOENT') throw error
298	  }
299	  ensureSymlink(link, target)
300	}
301	
302	/** Package names represented by owned symlinks below one fallback node_modules. */
303	function ownedPackageNames(modulesDir: string): string[] {
304	  return readdirSync(modulesDir, { withFileTypes: true }).flatMap((entry) => {
305	    if (entry.name.startsWith('@') && entry.isDirectory()) {
306	      return readdirSync(join(modulesDir, entry.name), { withFileTypes: true })
307	        .filter(child => child.isSymbolicLink())
308	        .map(child => `${entry.name}/${child.name}`)
309	    }
310	    return entry.isSymbolicLink() ? [entry.name] : []
311	  })
312	}
313	
314	/** Remove an obsolete owned target and its profile projection when still connected. */
315	function removeProfileSymlink(profileModulesDir: string, ownedModulesDir: string, packageName: string): void {
316	  const ownedLink = join(ownedModulesDir, packageName)
317	  const profileLink = join(profileModulesDir, packageName)
318	  try {
319	    if (lstatSync(profileLink).isSymbolicLink() && symlinkPointsTo(profileLink, ownedLink)) unlinkSync(profileLink)
320	  } catch (error) {
321	    /* v8 ignore next -- a non-ENOENT lstat failure requires a host filesystem fault */
322	    if ((error as NodeJS.ErrnoException).code !== 'ENOENT') throw error
323	  }
324	  try {
325	    unlinkSync(ownedLink)
326	  } catch (error) {
327	    /* v8 ignore next -- concurrent identical cleanup may remove the link first */
328	    if ((error as NodeJS.ErrnoException).code !== 'ENOENT') throw error
329	  }
330	}
331	
332	interface ModuleProxyManifest {
333	  name: string
334	  version: string
335	  private: true
336	  type: 'module'
337	  exports: Record<string, string>
338	  dsh: { moduleFallback: { targets: Record<string, string> } }
339	}
340	
341	interface ModuleProxyRecord {
342	  version?: unknown
343	  dsh?: { moduleFallback?: { targets?: unknown } }
344	}
345	
346	/** Return whether the process reads application modules from pkg's virtual filesystem. */
347	function isPackagedExecutable(): boolean {
348	  return (process as NodeJS.Process & { pkg?: unknown }).pkg !== undefined
349	}
350	
351	/** Resolve one available explicit package export under Node ESM import conditions. */
352	function packageEntryFromPackage(
353	  packageName: string,
354	  packageDir: string,
355	  declared: ResolvePackageManifest['exports'],
356	  subpath: string,
357	): string | undefined {
358	  let candidates: string[] | void
359	  try {
360	    candidates = resolvePackage({ name: packageName, exports: declared }, subpath)
361	  } catch (error) {
362	    if ((error as Error).message.startsWith('No known conditions for ')) return undefined
363	    const specifier = subpath === '.' ? packageName : packageName + subpath.slice(1)
364	    throw new Error(`dsh: cannot resolve ESM export ${specifier} from installed package ${packageName}`, { cause: error })
365	  }
366	  for (const candidate of candidates ?? []) {
367	    const target = candidate
368	    const entry = resolve(packageDir, target)
369	    const relativeEntry = relative(packageDir, entry)
370	    if (!target.startsWith('./') || /^\.\.(?:[\\/]|$)/u.test(relativeEntry)) {
371	      throw new Error(`dsh: installed package ${packageName} export ${subpath} resolves outside its package: ${target}`)
372	    }
373	    if (existsSync(entry) && statSync(entry).isFile()) return pathToFileURL(entry).href
374	  }
375	  return undefined
376	}
377	
378	/** Resolve every explicit ESM runtime export that an out-of-tree plugin can import. */
379	function packageProxySource(
380	  packageName: string,
381	  packageDir: string,
382	): { version: string; targets: Record<string, string> } {
383	  const manifest = JSON.parse(readFileSync(join(packageDir, 'package.json'), 'utf8')) as {
384	    bin?: unknown
385	    exports?: unknown
386	    main?: unknown
387	    types?: unknown
388	    typings?: unknown
389	    version?: unknown
390	  }
391	  if (typeof manifest.version !== 'string' || manifest.version.length === 0) {
392	    throw new Error(`dsh: installed package ${packageName} must declare a non-empty version`)
393	  }
394	  const declared = manifest.exports
395	  if (declared === undefined) {
396	    const main = typeof manifest.main === 'string' && manifest.main.length > 0 ? manifest.main : undefined
397	    const entry = join(packageDir, main ?? 'index')
398	    try {
399	      const resolved = createRequire(join(packageDir, 'package.json')).resolve(entry)
400	      return { version: manifest.version, targets: { '.': pathToFileURL(resolved).href } }
401	    } catch (error) {
402	      if (main === undefined
403	        && (manifest.bin !== undefined || manifest.types !== undefined || manifest.typings !== undefined)) {
404	        return { version: manifest.version, targets: {} }
405	      }
406	      throw new Error(`dsh: installed package ${packageName} main entry is missing at ${entry}`, { cause: error })
407	    }
408	  }
409	  const subpaths = declared !== null && typeof declared === 'object' && !Array.isArray(declared)
410	    && Object.keys(declared).some(key => key.startsWith('.'))
411	    ? Object.keys(declared).filter(key => key === '.' || (
412	      key.startsWith('./') && !key.includes('*') && !key.endsWith('/') && key !== './package.json'
413	    ))
414	    : ['.']
415	  const targets: Record<string, string> = {}
416	  for (const subpath of subpaths) {
417	    const target = packageEntryFromPackage(
418	      packageName,
419	      packageDir,
420	      declared as ResolvePackageManifest['exports'],
421	      subpath,
422	    )
423	    if (target !== undefined) targets[subpath] = target
424	  }
425	  return { version: manifest.version, targets }
426	}
427	
428	/**
429	 * Materialize a real package proxy whose exports retain pkg's virtual module
430	 * URL. Files outside the executable cannot traverse a symlink into
431	 * `/snapshot`, while an ESM re-export can import that URL and preserves the
432	 * executable's single module instance for out-of-tree plugin peers.
433	 */
434	function ensureModuleProxy(
435	  link: string,
436	  packageName: string,
437	  version: string,
438	  targets: Record<string, string>,
439	): void {
440	  const proxyExports = Object.fromEntries(
441	    Object.keys(targets).map((subpath, index) => [subpath, `./entry-${index}.js`]),
442	  )
443	  const manifest: ModuleProxyManifest = {
444	    name: packageName,
445	    version,
446	    private: true,
447	    type: 'module',
448	    exports: proxyExports,
449	    dsh: { moduleFallback: { targets } },
450	  }
451	  let stat
452	  try {
453	    stat = lstatSync(link)
454	  } catch {
455	    stat = undefined
456	  }
457	  if (stat?.isSymbolicLink()) {
458	    unlinkSync(link)
459	    stat = undefined
460	  }
461	  if (stat !== undefined) {
462	    const existing = readModuleProxyRecord(link)
463	    if (existing?.dsh?.moduleFallback?.targets === undefined) {
464	      throw new Error(`dsh: ${link} exists and is not a dsh-managed module proxy; remove it so dsh can manage the installation fallback`)
465	    }
466	    if (existing.version === version
467	      && JSON.stringify(existing.dsh.moduleFallback.targets) === JSON.stringify(targets)
468	      && Object.keys(targets).every((_, index) => existsSync(join(link, `entry-${index}.js`)))) return
469	    rmSync(link, { recursive: true })
470	  }
471	  mkdirSync(link, { recursive: true })
472	  writeFileSync(join(link, 'package.json'), JSON.stringify(manifest, undefined, 2) + '\n')
473	  for (const [index, target] of Object.values(targets).entries()) {
474	    const specifier = JSON.stringify(target)
475	    writeFileSync(
476	      join(link, `entry-${index}.js`),
477	      `export * from ${specifier}\nimport * as target from ${specifier}\nexport default target.default\n`,
478	    )
479	  }
480	}
481	
482	type ModuleFallbackEntry =
483	  | { kind: 'symlink'; packageName: string; packageDir: string }
484	  | { kind: 'proxy'; packageName: string; version: string; targets: Record<string, string> }
485	
486	/** Read one package manifest used while traversing a module-fallback dependency graph. */
487	function readModuleFallbackManifest(anchor: string): ProfileManifest {
488	  return JSON.parse(readFileSync(anchor, 'utf8')) as ProfileManifest
489	}
490	
491	/** Return dependency names that may be imported by a loader-visible plugin. */
492	function profileDependencyNames(manifest: ProfileManifest): string[] {
493	  return [...Object.keys(manifest.dependencies ?? {}), ...Object.keys(manifest.peerDependencies ?? {})]
494	}
495	
496	/** Resolve the installation generation that every profile must find through the fallback directory. */
497	function resolveModuleFallbackEntries(
498	  installAnchor: string,
499	): { entries: ModuleFallbackEntry[]; packageNames: ReadonlySet<string> } {
500	  const appManifest = readModuleFallbackManifest(installAnchor)
501	  const links = new Map<string, string>()
502	  /* v8 ignore next -- a real app manifest always declares its name */
503	  if (appManifest.name !== undefined) links.set(appManifest.name, dirname(installAnchor))
504	  // BFS over the resolvable dependency graph; the visited set is the link
505	  // map itself (first resolution wins, matching Node's own nearest-wins).
506	  const queue: { anchor: string; manifest: ProfileManifest }[] = [{ anchor: installAnchor, manifest: appManifest }]
507	  for (let next = queue.shift(); next !== undefined; next = queue.shift()) {
508	    // Peer dependencies participate: Service Definition packages (dsh-subprocess,
509	    // dsh-compaction, ...) are peers of their implementations, never plain
510	    // dependencies, yet out-of-tree plugins import them directly.
511	    /* v8 ignore next -- a real app manifest always declares dependencies */
512	    for (const dep of profileDependencyNames(next.manifest)) {
513	      if (links.has(dep)) continue
514	      const dir = packageDirFromAnchor(next.anchor, dep)
515	      // A declared-but-uninstalled dependency cannot be a loader-visible
516	      // plugin; skip it rather than fail the whole boot.
517	      if (dir === undefined) continue
518	      links.set(dep, dir)
519	      const manifestPath = join(dir, 'package.json')
520	      queue.push({ anchor: manifestPath, manifest: readModuleFallbackManifest(manifestPath) })
521	    }
522	  }
523	  const entries = !isPackagedExecutable()
524	    ? [...links].map(([packageName, packageDir]) => ({ kind: 'symlink' as const, packageName, packageDir }))
525	    : [...links].flatMap(([packageName, packageDir]) => {
526	      const source = packageProxySource(packageName, packageDir)
527	      return Object.keys(source.targets).length === 0
528	        ? []
529	        : [{ kind: 'proxy' as const, packageName, version: source.version, targets: source.targets }]
530	    })
531	  return { entries, packageNames: new Set(links.keys()) }
532	}
533	
534	/** Return whether one existing fallback entry already matches its resolved installation generation. */
535	function moduleFallbackEntryCurrent(modulesDir: string, entry: ModuleFallbackEntry): boolean {
536	  const link = join(modulesDir, entry.packageName)
537	  try {
538	    const stat = lstatSync(link)
539	    if (entry.kind === 'symlink') {
540	      return stat.isSymbolicLink() && readlinkSync(link) === entry.packageDir
541	    }
542	    if (!stat.isDirectory()) return false
543	    const existing = readModuleProxyRecord(link)
544	    return existing?.version === entry.version
545	      && JSON.stringify(existing.dsh?.moduleFallback?.targets) === JSON.stringify(entry.targets)
546	      && Object.keys(entry.targets).every((_, index) => existsSync(join(link, `entry-${index}.js`)))
547	  } catch {
548	    return false
549	  }
550	}
551	
552	/** Return whether every required fallback entry is already ready for this installation. */
553	function moduleFallbackCurrent(modulesDir: string, entries: readonly ModuleFallbackEntry[]): boolean {
554	  return entries.every(entry => moduleFallbackEntryCurrent(modulesDir, entry))
555	}
556	
557	/** Inputs for {@link healProfilesModuleFallback}. */
558	export interface ProfileModuleFallbackOptions {
559	  /** Absolute package.json path of the running dsh installation. */
560	  installAnchor: string
561	  /** Loaded profile whose selected bundles may carry profile-local plugins. */
562	  profile?: Profile
563	  /** Harness home; defaults to {@link resolveDshHome}. */
564	  home?: string
565	}
566	
567	/**
568	 * Maintain module fallbacks for one profile launch. The shared
569	 * `$DSH_HOME/profiles/node_modules` mirrors the dsh installation dependency
570	 * closure. Plain Node writes symlinks; a packaged executable writes ESM
571	 * proxies under a cross-process lock because operating-system links cannot
572	 * enter pkg's virtual filesystem. Missing packages carried only by selected
573	 * bundles are linked through a profile-owned directory into that profile's
574	 * `node_modules`; pnpm-managed entries remain authoritative, and another
575	 * profile's links cannot change its resolution.
576	 * @param options - installation anchor, optional loaded profile, and Harness home.
577	 * @returns settlement after the shared fallback and profile-local links are current.
578	 */
579	export async function healProfilesModuleFallback(options: ProfileModuleFallbackOptions): Promise<void> {
580	  const { installAnchor, profile, home = resolveDshHome() } = options
581	  const profilesDir = join(home, PROFILES_DIR)
582	  const modulesDir = join(profilesDir, 'node_modules')
583	  mkdirSync(modulesDir, { recursive: true })
584	  const { entries, packageNames } = resolveModuleFallbackEntries(installAnchor)
585	  if (!moduleFallbackCurrent(modulesDir, entries)) {
586	    await withFileLock(modulesDir, () => {
587	      if (!moduleFallbackCurrent(modulesDir, entries)) healProfilesModuleFallbackLocked(entries, modulesDir)
588	      return Promise.resolve()
589	    })
590	  }
591	  if (profile !== undefined) healProfileModuleFallback(profile, packageNames)
592	}
593	
594	/** Heal one module-fallback generation while the cross-process writer lock is held. */
595	function healProfilesModuleFallbackLocked(entries: readonly ModuleFallbackEntry[], modulesDir: string): void {
596	  for (const entry of entries) {
597	    const link = join(modulesDir, entry.packageName)
598	    mkdirSync(dirname(link), { recursive: true })
599	    if (entry.kind === 'proxy') {
600	      ensureModuleProxy(link, entry.packageName, entry.version, entry.targets)
601	    } else {
602	      ensureSymlink(link, entry.packageDir)
603	    }
604	  }
605	}
606	
607	/** Collect the first resolvable package directory for each dependency name. */
608	function dependencyClosure(
609	  anchors: readonly string[], reserved: ReadonlySet<string>,
610	  exclude: (candidate: string, packageName: string) => boolean,
611	): Map<string, string> {
612	  const links = new Map<string, string>()
613	  const visited = new Set(reserved)
614	  for (const anchor of anchors) {
615	    const canonicalAnchor = realpathSync.native(anchor)
616	    const manifest = readModuleFallbackManifest(canonicalAnchor)
617	    /* v8 ignore next -- an installable package manifest always declares its name */
618	    if (manifest.name === undefined) continue
619	    if (!visited.has(manifest.name)) {
620	      visited.add(manifest.name)
621	      links.set(manifest.name, dirname(canonicalAnchor))
622	    }
623	    const queue: { anchor: string; manifest: ProfileManifest }[] = [{ anchor: canonicalAnchor, manifest }]
624	    for (let next = queue.shift(); next !== undefined; next = queue.shift()) {
625	      // Service Provider packages commonly expose Service Definitions as peers.
626	      /* v8 ignore next -- an installable package manifest always declares dependencies or peers */
627	      for (const dep of profileDependencyNames(next.manifest)) {
628	        if (visited.has(dep)) continue
629	        const dir = packageDirFromAnchor(next.anchor, dep, exclude)
630	        // A declared-but-uninstalled dependency cannot be loader-visible.
631	        if (dir === undefined) continue
632	        visited.add(dep)
633	        links.set(dep, dir)
634	        const manifestPath = join(dir, 'package.json')
635	        queue.push({ anchor: manifestPath, manifest: readModuleFallbackManifest(manifestPath) })
636	      }
637	    }
638	  }
639	  return links
640	}
641	
642	/** Reconcile packages carried only by selected bundles into one profile. */
643	function healProfileModuleFallback(profile: Profile, installationPackageNames: ReadonlySet<string>): void {
644	  const profileModulesDir = join(profile.dir, 'node_modules')
645	  const ownedModulesDir = join(profile.dir, PROFILE_MODULE_FALLBACK_DIR, 'node_modules')
646	  mkdirSync(profileModulesDir, { recursive: true })
647	  mkdirSync(ownedModulesDir, { recursive: true })
648	  const bundleAnchors = profile.layers
649	    .filter(layer => !installationPackageNames.has(layer.packageName))
650	    .map(layer => join(layer.packageDir, 'package.json'))
651	  const bundleLinks = dependencyClosure(bundleAnchors, installationPackageNames, (candidate, packageName) => {
652	    const profileLink = join(profileModulesDir, packageName)
653	    if (canonicalLinkPath(candidate) !== canonicalLinkPath(profileLink)) return false
654	    try {
655	      return lstatSync(profileLink).isSymbolicLink()
656	        && symlinkPointsTo(profileLink, join(ownedModulesDir, packageName))
657	    } catch (error) {
658	      // A concurrent cleanup may remove the projection after package discovery.
659	      /* v8 ignore next 2 -- a non-ENOENT lstat failure requires a host filesystem fault */
660	      if ((error as NodeJS.ErrnoException).code === 'ENOENT') return true
661	      /* v8 ignore next -- see the host-filesystem exception above */
662	      throw error
663	    }
664	  })
665	  for (const layer of profile.layers) bundleLinks.delete(layer.packageName)
666	  for (const packageName of ownedPackageNames(ownedModulesDir)) {
667	    if (!bundleLinks.has(packageName)) removeProfileSymlink(profileModulesDir, ownedModulesDir, packageName)
668	  }
669	  for (const [packageName, target] of bundleLinks) {
670	    const ownedLink = join(ownedModulesDir, packageName)
671	    mkdirSync(dirname(ownedLink), { recursive: true })
672	    ensureSymlink(ownedLink, target)
673	    const profileLink = join(profileModulesDir, packageName)
674	    mkdirSync(dirname(profileLink), { recursive: true })
675	    ensureProfileSymlink(profileLink, ownedLink)
676	  }
677	}
678	
679	/**
680	 * Read a profile's manifest.
681	 * @param binName - the diagnostic prefix on the thrown error.
682	 * @param dir - the profile directory.
683	 * @returns the parsed manifest.
684	 */
685	export function readProfileManifest(binName: string, dir: string): ProfileManifest {
686	  const path = join(dir, 'package.json')
687	  let raw: string
688	  try {
689	    raw = readFileSync(path, 'utf8')
690	  } catch (error) {
691	    throw new Error(`${binName}: failed to read profile manifest ${path}: ${String(error)}`)
692	  }
693	  // The field checks below validate the file data before trusting the parse type.
694	  const parsed = JSON.parse(raw) as ProfileManifest | null
695	  if (parsed === null || typeof parsed !== 'object' || Array.isArray(parsed)) {
696	    throw new Error(`${binName}: profile manifest ${path} must hold a JSON object`)
697	  }
698	  return parsed
699	}
700	
701	/**
702	 * Write a profile's manifest back (2-space JSON, trailing newline).
703	 * @param dir - the profile directory.
704	 * @param manifest - the manifest value to persist.
705	 */
706	export function writeProfileManifest(dir: string, manifest: ProfileManifest): void {
707	  writeFileSync(join(dir, 'package.json'), JSON.stringify(manifest, undefined, 2) + '\n')
708	}
709	
710	/** Return whether two bundle lists have the same values in the same order. */
711	function sameBundles(left: readonly string[], right: readonly string[]): boolean {
712	  return left.length === right.length && left.every((value, index) => value === right[index])
713	}
714	
715	/**
716	 * Normalize an exact installation-owned bundle tuple to its shipped template,
717	 * or add the shipped reload default to an exact current tuple. A changed value
718	 * is written back during profile loading while every other manifest field is
719	 * preserved; any other bundle list is user-owned and remains untouched.
720	 */
721	function normalizeShippedProfile(name: string, dir: string, manifest: ProfileManifest): ProfileManifest {
722	  const installationOwned = INSTALLATION_OWNED_PROFILE_TUPLES[name]
723	  const template = PROFILE_TEMPLATES[name]
724	  const bundles = manifest.dsh?.profile?.bundles
725	  if (template === undefined || bundles === undefined) return manifest
726	  const isRetiredTuple = installationOwned !== undefined && sameBundles(bundles, installationOwned)
727	  const isCurrentTuple = sameBundles(bundles, template.bundles)
728	  const needsReloadDefault = manifest.dsh?.profile?.patchReload === undefined && isCurrentTuple
729	  if (!isRetiredTuple && !needsReloadDefault) return manifest
730	  const normalized: ProfileManifest = {
731	    ...manifest,
732	    dsh: {
733	      ...manifest.dsh,
734	      profile: {
735	        ...manifest.dsh?.profile,
736	        bundles: [...template.bundles],
737	        patchReload: manifest.dsh?.profile?.patchReload ?? template.patchReload,
738	      },
739	    },
740	  }
741	  writeProfileManifest(dir, normalized)
742	  return normalized
743	}
744	
745	/**
746	 * Resolve a package's root directory from one anchor without depending on the
747	 * package exporting `./package.json` (`require.resolve` would need that):
748	 * probe the require resolution paths for a directory holding the named
749	 * manifest. This is Node's own node_modules lookup order, so the result
750	 * matches what the Loader would import from the same anchor, and
751	 * `existsSync` follows the symlinks pnpm's isolated layout uses.
752	 */
753	function packageDirFromAnchor(
754	  anchor: string, packageName: string,
755	  exclude: (candidate: string, packageName: string) => boolean = () => false,
756	): string | undefined {
757	  // resolve.paths returns null only for builtins, which no bundle name is.
758	  /* v8 ignore next */
759	  for (const searchPath of createRequire(anchor).resolve.paths(packageName) ?? []) {
760	    const candidate = join(searchPath, packageName)
761	    if (existsSync(join(candidate, 'package.json')) && !exclude(candidate, packageName)) return candidate
762	  }
763	  return undefined
764	}
765	
766	/**
767	 * Resolve one bundle package's directory: installation anchor first, then the
768	 * profile directory. The installation-first order is the contract that
769	 * `@deepseek-ai/dsh-base` (and every other in-box bundle) always comes from
770	 * the same installation as the running dsh, never from a profile-local copy.
771	 * Resolution does not require the package to export `./package.json`.
772	 * @param binName - the diagnostic prefix on the thrown error.
773	 * @param packageName - the bundle's package name from `dsh.profile.bundles`.
774	 * @param installAnchor - absolute path of a file inside the dsh app package (its package.json).
775	 * @param profileDir - the profile directory (second anchor).
776	 * @returns the bundle package's absolute directory.
777	 */
778	export function resolveBundleDir(
779	  binName: string, packageName: string, installAnchor: string, profileDir: string,
780	): string {
781	  for (const anchor of [installAnchor, join(profileDir, 'package.json')]) {
782	    const dir = packageDirFromAnchor(anchor, packageName)
783	    if (dir !== undefined) return dir
784	  }
785	  throw new Error(
786	    `${binName}: cannot resolve profile bundle ${JSON.stringify(packageName)} from the dsh installation or ${profileDir}; `
787	    + `run 'dsh plugin --profile ${basename(profileDir)} install' if its dependency is not installed`,
788	  )
789	}
790	
791	/**
792	 * Load a profile: resolve every `dsh.profile.bundles` entry to its patch
793	 * layer and parse the profile's own patch file. A listed bundle without a
794	 * `dsh.bundle` manifest fails loud — naming a bundle-less package as a layer
795	 * is a misconfiguration, not "no patches".
796	 * @param binName - the diagnostic prefix on thrown errors.
797	 * @param name - the profile name.
798	 * @param installAnchor - absolute path of the dsh app's package.json (first resolution anchor).
799	 * @param home - the Harness home; defaults to {@link resolveDshHome}.
800	 * @param options - `userLayer: false` skips reading `cordis.patch.yml`, so a
801	 * bundles-only consumer (`--dump-default-config`, a recovery diagnostic)
802	 * cannot fail on a broken user layer.
803	 * @returns the loaded profile (empty `patches` when the user layer is skipped).
804	 */
805	export function loadProfile(
806	  binName: string, name: string, installAnchor: string, home: string = resolveDshHome(),
807	  options: { userLayer?: boolean } = {},
808	): Profile {
809	  const dir = resolveProfileDir(name, home)
810	  if (!existsSync(join(dir, 'package.json'))) {
811	    const template = PROFILE_TEMPLATES[name]
812	    if (template === undefined) {
813	      throw new Error(
814	        `${binName}: profile ${JSON.stringify(name)} does not exist; create it with 'dsh plugin --profile ${name} add <package>'`,
815	      )
816	    }
817	    initProfile(dir, template.bundles, template.patchReload)
818	  }
819	  const manifest = normalizeShippedProfile(name, dir, readProfileManifest(binName, dir))
820	  // A hand-written profile manifest may omit the dsh section entirely.
821	  const bundles = manifest.dsh?.profile?.bundles ?? []
822	  const rawPatchReload: unknown = manifest.dsh?.profile?.patchReload
823	  if (rawPatchReload !== undefined && rawPatchReload !== 'live' && rawPatchReload !== 'startup') {
824	    throw new Error(
825	      `${binName}: profile manifest ${join(dir, 'package.json')} dsh.profile.patchReload must be "live" or "startup"`,
826	    )
827	  }
828	  const patchReload = rawPatchReload ?? DEFAULT_PROFILE_PATCH_RELOAD
829	  const layers = bundles.map((packageName): ProfileLayer => {
830	    const packageDir = resolveBundleDir(binName, packageName, installAnchor, dir)
831	    const bundleManifest = JSON.parse(readFileSync(join(packageDir, 'package.json'), 'utf8')) as ProfileManifest
832	    const declared = bundleManifest.dsh?.bundle?.patch
833	    if (declared === undefined) {
834	      throw new Error(`${binName}: profile bundle ${JSON.stringify(packageName)} declares no dsh.bundle in its package.json`)
835	    }
836	    const patchPath = join(packageDir, declared)
837	    return { packageName, packageDir, patchPath, patches: loadOverlayPatches(binName, patchPath) }
838	  })
839	  const patchPath = join(dir, PROFILE_PATCH_FILENAME)
840	  const patches = options.userLayer !== false && existsSync(patchPath)
841	    ? loadOverlayPatches(binName, patchPath)
842	    : []
843	  return { name, dir, layers, patchPath, patches, patchReload }
844	}
845	
846	/**
847	 * Compose patch layers into the effective entry list over an empty root —
848	 * the same single `applyEntryPatches` call the boot include makes, so flag
849	 * derivation and config dumps see exactly what mounts.
850	 * @param layers - patch lists in application order.
851	 * @param warn - sink for skipped-patch diagnostics; defaults to silent (boot repeats them).
852	 * @returns the composed entry list.
853	 */
854	export function composeEntries(
855	  layers: readonly PatchOptions[][], warn: (message: string) => void = () => {},
856	): EntryOptions[] {
857	  return applyEntryPatches([], structuredClone(layers.flat()), (message: string, ...args: unknown[]) => {
858	    let index = 0
859	    warn(message.replace(/%C/g, () => JSON.stringify(args[index++])))
860	  })
861	}

1	/**
2	 * Commander adapter for the `dsh` command line.
3	 *
4	 * The launcher parses only what it owns — which profile to boot, which extra
5	 * patch overlays to apply, and the config dumps — and hands **everything after
6	 * its own flags** to the booted tree verbatim, where injected app plugins parse
7	 * their own flag families and print their own `--help` (see
8	 * `@deepseek-ai/dsh-cmdline`). Launcher flags therefore come first: the first
9	 * token this parser does not recognize starts the inner arguments, so
10	 * `dsh --profile tui --resume abc` boots the tui profile with `--resume abc`,
11	 * and `dsh --profile web -h` prints the web app's help, not this one's.
12	 *
13	 * `web` is a hardcoded alias for `--profile web`; `plugin` manages a profile's
14	 * plugin dependencies by forwarding to pnpm.
15	 * @module @deepseek-ai/dsh/args
16	 */
17	
18	import { Command, CommanderError } from 'commander'
19	
20	/** Boot a named profile and hand it the invocation's inner arguments. */
21	interface ProfileInvocation {
22	  mode: 'profile'
23	  profile: string
24	  /** Extra patch-list overlays applied after the profile's own layer, in argv order. */
25	  patches: string[]
26	  /** Everything after the launcher's own flags, verbatim, for injected app plugins. */
27	  args: string[]
28	}
29	
30	/** Print a composed profile tree and exit without booting. */
31	interface DumpConfigInvocation {
32	  mode: 'dump-config'
33	  profile: string
34	  /** Omit the profile's user layer and --patch overlays; print bundle layers only. */
35	  defaultOnly: boolean
36	  patches: string[]
37	}
38	
39	/** Manage a profile's plugins: forward `args` to pnpm inside the profile directory. */
40	interface PluginInvocation {
41	  mode: 'plugin'
42	  profile: string
43	  /** Raw pnpm arguments, verbatim. */
44	  args: string[]
45	}
46	
47	/** The resolved `dsh` invocation. Help, version, and errors exit inside {@link parseDshArgs}. */
48	export type DshInvocation = ProfileInvocation | DumpConfigInvocation | PluginInvocation
49	
50	/** Launcher flags shared by the default command and the `web` alias. */
51	interface BootOptions {
52	  patch?: string[]
53	  dumpConfig?: boolean
54	  dumpDefaultConfig?: boolean
55	}
56	
57	/**
58	 * Repeatable single-value collector: `--patch a.yml --patch b.yml`. Never
59	 * variadic — a variadic `--patch` would swallow the inner arguments.
60	 */
61	const collect = (value: string, previous: string[] = []): string[] => [...previous, value]
62	
63	/** The launcher's own help text; each app prints its own. */
64	const HELP_EXAMPLES = `
65	Examples:
66	  dsh --profile web                          boot the web profile (same as: dsh web)
67	  dsh --profile headless "run the tests"     answer one task, print the result, and exit
68	  dsh --profile tui --patch ./extra.yml      boot a custom profile with one extra overlay
69	  dsh --profile tui --resume <session>       arguments after the launcher flags reach the app
70	  dsh --profile web --help                   the web app's own flags and help
71	  dsh plugin --profile tui add <package>     install a plugin into the tui profile
72	`
73	
74	/**
75	 * Resolve a boot or dump invocation from the launcher flags and the leftover
76	 * inner arguments.
77	 * @param program - the command whose options were parsed (the root, or the `web` alias).
78	 * @param profile - the profile these flags boot.
79	 * @param options - the launcher flags commander collected.
80	 * @param args - the leftover arguments, in argv order.
81	 * @returns the resolved invocation.
82	 */
83	function resolveBoot(program: Command, profile: string, options: BootOptions, args: string[]): DshInvocation {
84	  const patches = options.patch ?? []
85	  if (patches.includes('')) program.error('error: --patch needs a path')
86	  if (options.dumpConfig !== true && options.dumpDefaultConfig !== true) {
87	    return { mode: 'profile', profile, patches, args }
88	  }
89	  if (options.dumpConfig === true && options.dumpDefaultConfig === true) {
90	    program.error('error: --dump-config and --dump-default-config are mutually exclusive')
91	  }
92	  // The dump is boot-free: it never runs app command-line providers, so it
93	  // cannot show what those flags would decide, and printing a tree that differs
94	  // from the same invocation's boot would mislead.
95	  if (args.length > 0) {
96	    program.error(`error: config dumps take no app arguments, got ${args.map(argument => JSON.stringify(argument)).join(' ')}`)
97	  }
98	  const defaultOnly = options.dumpDefaultConfig === true
99	  if (defaultOnly && patches.length > 0) {
100	    program.error('error: --dump-default-config prints the bundle layers and takes no --patch')
101	  }
102	  return { mode: 'dump-config', profile, defaultOnly, patches }
103	}
104	
105	/**
106	 * Resolve argv into one invocation, or print and exit for help, version, or an
107	 * error.
108	 * @param argv - arguments after the Node binary and script.
109	 * @param version - version string printed by `--version`.
110	 * @returns the resolved invocation.
111	 */
112	export function parseDshArgs(argv: readonly string[], version: string): DshInvocation {
113	  let resolved: DshInvocation | undefined
114	  // Annotated, not inferred: the actions below call back into `program`, and an
115	  // inferred type would be circular through its own chain.
116	  const program: Command = new Command()
117	  program
118	    .name('dsh')
119	    .version(version, '-V, --version', 'output the version number')
120	    .description('dsh: boot a DeepSeek Harness profile — an ordered stack of plugin-bundle patch layers under your own overrides.')
121	    .addHelpText('after', HELP_EXAMPLES)
122	    .exitOverride()
123	    // The launcher's flags come first and end at the first token it does not
124	    // know; everything from there on belongs to the booted app, including
125	    // its -h. `dsh -h` with no profile still prints this help, below.
126	    .helpOption(false)
127	    .allowUnknownOption()
128	    .passThroughOptions()
129	    .enablePositionalOptions()
130	    .argument('[args...]', 'arguments for the booted profile\'s app (see: dsh --profile <name> --help)')
131	    .option('--profile <name>', 'the profile under $DSH_HOME/profiles to boot')
132	    .option('--patch <path>', 'extra patch-list overlay applied after the profile layer (repeatable)', collect)
133	    .option('--dump-config', 'print the composed profile tree and exit')
134	    .option('--dump-default-config', 'print the profile tree without its user layer or --patch overlays and exit')
135	    .action((args: string[], options: BootOptions & { profile?: string }) => {
136	      // With the app owning -h, the launcher's own help is what a bare
137	      // `dsh -h` (no profile to hand it to) must print.
138	      if (options.profile === undefined) {
139	        if (args.some(argument => argument === '-h' || argument === '--help')) program.help()
140	        program.error('error: --profile <name> is required')
141	      }
142	      const profile = options.profile
143	      if (profile === '') program.error('error: --profile needs a name')
144	      resolved = resolveBoot(program, profile, options, args)
145	    })
146	
147	  /** Reject parent options supplied before a subcommand. */
148	  const rejectParentOptions = (command: string): void => {
149	    const parent = program.opts<BootOptions & { profile?: string }>()
150	    if (parent.profile !== undefined || parent.patch !== undefined
151	      || parent.dumpConfig !== undefined || parent.dumpDefaultConfig !== undefined) {
152	      program.error(`error: ${command} takes none of parent --profile, --patch, --dump-config, or --dump-default-config`)
153	    }
154	  }
155	
156	  const web = program.command('web').description('boot the web profile (alias of --profile web); the web app\'s own flags follow')
157	  web
158	    .helpOption(false)
159	    .allowUnknownOption()
160	    .passThroughOptions()
161	    .enablePositionalOptions()
162	    .argument('[args...]', 'arguments for the web app (see: dsh web --help)')
163	    .option('--patch <path>', 'extra patch-list overlay applied after the profile layer (repeatable)', collect)
164	    .option('--dump-config', 'print the composed web-profile tree (with the user layer and any --patch) and exit')
165	    .option('--dump-default-config', 'print the web profile\'s bundle layers (no user layer) and exit')
166	    .action((args: string[], options: BootOptions) => {
167	      rejectParentOptions('web')
168	      resolved = resolveBoot(web, 'web', options, args)
169	    })
170	
171	  const plugin = program.command('plugin').description('manage a profile\'s plugins by forwarding the remaining arguments to pnpm in the profile directory')
172	  plugin
173	    .requiredOption('--profile <name>', 'the profile whose plugins to manage (initialized on first use)')
174	    .allowUnknownOption()
175	    .argument('[args...]', 'pnpm arguments, forwarded verbatim (add <pkg>, remove <pkg>, why <pkg>, ...)')
176	    .action((args: string[], options: { profile: string }) => {
177	      rejectParentOptions('plugin')
178	      if (options.profile === '') program.error('error: --profile needs a name')
179	      if (args.length === 0) program.error('error: plugin needs pnpm arguments to forward (e.g. add <package>)')
180	      resolved = { mode: 'plugin', profile: options.profile, args }
181	    })
182	
183	  try {
184	    program.parse(argv, { from: 'user' })
185	  } catch (error) {
186	    return process.exit(error instanceof CommanderError ? error.exitCode : 1)
187	  }
188	  /* v8 ignore next -- an action resolves or Commander throws */
189	  if (resolved === undefined) throw new Error('dsh: no invocation resolved')
190	  return resolved
191	}

12	import { parseDshArgs } from './args.ts'
13	
14	// Both the source tree (apps/cli/src) and the bundled bin (apps/cli/lib) sit
15	// one directory under apps/cli, so the checked-in manifest resolves with the
16	// same relative hop from either artifact.
17	function readVersion(): string {
18	  const manifest = JSON.parse(
19	    readFileSync(fileURLToPath(new URL('../package.json', import.meta.url)), 'utf8'),
20	  ) as { version?: unknown }
21	  return typeof manifest.version === 'string' ? manifest.version : '0.0.0'
22	}

27	  case 'profile': {
28	    const { runProfile } = await import('./profile-boot.ts')
29	    await runProfile({
30	      environment: loadLayeredEnv('dsh'),
31	      profile: invocation.profile,
32	      patchFiles: invocation.patches,
33	      args: invocation.args,
34	    })
35	    break
36	  }
37	  case 'plugin': {
38	    const { runPlugin } = await import('./plugin.ts')
39	    process.exit(runPlugin(invocation.profile, invocation.args))

42	  case 'dump-config': {

1	/**
2	 * Shared profile boot for every `dsh` surface: resolve the profile, stack its
3	 * patch layers (bundle layers in `dsh.profile.bundles` order, the profile's
4	 * own `cordis.patch.yml`, `--patch` overlays, the telemetry switch), mount the
5	 * tree over the profile's empty root config, apply its selected patch-reload
6	 * lifecycle, and wire fail-loud plus bounded shutdown.
7	 *
8	 * App flags are not the launcher's business: the invocation's inner arguments
9	 * are provided to the tree through `ctx.cmdlineArgs`, where any injected app
10	 * plugin may read the same immutable snapshot.
11	 * @module @deepseek-ai/dsh/profile-boot
12	 */
13	
14	import { writeFileSync } from 'node:fs'
15	import { join, resolve } from 'node:path'
16	import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url'
17	import { FiberState, type Context } from '@deepseek-ai/cordis'
18	import type { PatchOptions } from '@deepseek-ai/cordis-plugin-include'
19	import type { EntryOptions } from '@deepseek-ai/cordis-plugin-loader'
20	import {
21	  boot,
22	  composeEntries,
23	  healProfilesModuleFallback,
24	  installFailLoud,
25	  loadOptionalPatches,
26	  loadOverlayPatches,
27	  loadProfile,
28	  PROFILE_PATCH_FILENAME,
29	  watchUserPatches,
30	  type Profile,
31	} from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-app-boot'
32	import { resolveDshHome } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-home-paths'
33	import { installProxyFromEnvironment } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-http-proxy'
34	import { DSH_LAUNCH_ENVIRONMENT_KEY, type LaunchEnvironmentSnapshot } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-launch-environment'
35	import { provideCmdline, type AppReady } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-cmdline'
36	import { createProcessShutdown, type ProcessShutdown } from './process-shutdown.ts'
37	
38	const NAME = 'dsh'
39	
40	/** Launcher-owned readiness signal committed only after boot and host setup succeed. */
41	function createAppReady(): { service: AppReady; commit(): void } {
42	  let ready = false
43	  const listeners = new Set<() => void>()
44	  return {
45	    service: {
46	      onReady(listener) {
47	        if (ready) {
48	          listener()
49	          return () => {}
50	        }
51	        listeners.add(listener)
52	        return () => { listeners.delete(listener) }
53	      },
54	    },
55	    commit() {
56	      if (ready) return
57	      ready = true
58	      for (const listener of [...listeners]) listener()
59	      listeners.clear()
60	    },
61	  }
62	}
63	
64	/**
65	 * The home-level user patch layer (`$DSH_HOME/cordis.patch.yml`), applied
66	 * over every profile's own layer. Resolved per call, not at module load:
67	 * `$DSH_HOME` may be set by the test or launcher after import.
68	 * @returns the absolute patch-file path.
69	 */
70	export function homePatchPath(): string {
71	  return join(resolveDshHome(), PROFILE_PATCH_FILENAME)
72	}

74	/** Absolute path of this dsh installation's package.json (both anchors: src/ and lib/ sit one level under apps/cli). */
75	export const INSTALL_ANCHOR = fileURLToPath(new URL('../package.json', import.meta.url))
76	
77	/** The session-telemetry row id the DSH_TELEMETRY_DISABLED switch targets. */
78	const TELEMETRY_ROW_ID = 'session-telemetry-otel'
79	
80	/** The empty root entry list every profile tree patches over. */
81	const PROFILE_ROOT_CONFIG = `# dsh profile root — an empty entry list. The tree is composed as patches:
82	# each bundle in package.json's dsh.profile.bundles, then cordis.patch.yml, then any
83	# --patch overlays. Edit cordis.patch.yml, not this file.
84	[]
85	`
86	
87	/** Root config filename inside a profile directory. */
88	export const PROFILE_ROOT_FILENAME = 'cordis.yml'
89	
90	/**
91	 * Resolve the telemetry opt-out switch into its boot patch. ANY non-empty
92	 * value (including `'0'`/`'false'`) disables: a privacy switch prefers
93	 * off-by-mistake over on-by-mistake. A composition without the telemetry row
94	 * exports nothing, so the switch is then trivially satisfied and no patch is
95	 * generated — custom profiles need not mount telemetry to run with the
96	 * switch set.
97	 * @param disabledEnv - the raw `DSH_TELEMETRY_DISABLED` value (`undefined` when unset).
98	 * @param hasRow - whether the composition carries the telemetry row.
99	 * @returns the disable patch, or `undefined` when no hard-disable patch is required.
100	 */
101	export function resolveTelemetryPatch(disabledEnv: string | undefined, hasRow: boolean): PatchOptions | undefined {
102	  if ((disabledEnv ?? '') === '' || !hasRow) return undefined
103	  return { id: TELEMETRY_ROW_ID, disabled: true }
104	}
105	
106	/**
107	 * Load a resolved profile for `name` and (re)write the empty root config. The
108	 * root is always rewritten: the whole composition is patch layers, and the
109	 * vendored Loader's tree write-back (a plugin self-disposing persists the
110	 * current tree) can bake composed rows into this file — which would duplicate
111	 * every bundle insert on the next boot. The file exists on disk only because
112	 * the Loader needs a real include root to anchor `baseUrl` at the profile
113	 * directory (the config dump anchors on the same file, so both compose over
114	 * the identical base).
115	 * @param name - the profile name.
116	 * @param userLayer - `false` skips parsing `cordis.patch.yml` (the default dump).
117	 * @returns the loaded profile.
118	 */
119	export function prepareProfile(name: string, userLayer = true): Profile {
120	  const profile = loadProfile(NAME, name, INSTALL_ANCHOR, undefined, { userLayer })
121	  writeFileSync(join(profile.dir, PROFILE_ROOT_FILENAME), PROFILE_ROOT_CONFIG)
122	  return profile
123	}
124	
125	/** One profile's patch layers, in application order. */
126	interface ComposedProfile {
127	  profile: Profile
128	  /** Bundle layers concatenated — the part below the user layers on a live reload. */
129	  bundlePatches: PatchOptions[]
130	  /** The home-level user layer (`$DSH_HOME/cordis.patch.yml`), applied after the profile's own. */
131	  homePatches: PatchOptions[]
132	  /** Layers above the user layers on a live reload: `--patch` overlays and the telemetry switch. */
133	  overlays: PatchOptions[]
134	}
135	
136	/** The full patch stack of one composed profile, in application order. */
137	function allPatches(composed: ComposedProfile): PatchOptions[] {
138	  return [
139	    ...composed.bundlePatches,
140	    ...composed.profile.patches,
141	    ...composed.homePatches,
142	    ...composed.overlays,
143	  ]
144	}
145	
146	/**
147	 * Load `name` and compose its effective patch stack: bundle layers in
148	 * `dsh.profile.bundles` order (a base-backed profile gets the base bundle's
149	 * platform-gated shell rows), the profile's user layer, the home-level user
150	 * layer (`$DSH_HOME/cordis.patch.yml` — machine-local preferences that apply
151	 * to every profile, so it outranks the per-profile layer), `--patch` overlays,
152	 * then the telemetry switch.
153	 * @param name - the profile name.
154	 * @param patchFiles - `--patch` overlay paths, in argv order.
155	 * @returns the profile and its patch layers.
156	 */
157	async function composeProfile(
158	  name: string,
159	  patchFiles: readonly string[],
160	): Promise<ComposedProfile> {
161	  const profile = prepareProfile(name)
162	  await healProfilesModuleFallback({ installAnchor: INSTALL_ANCHOR, profile })
163	  const homePatches = loadOptionalPatches(NAME, homePatchPath()) ?? []
164	  const overlays = patchFiles.flatMap(file => loadOverlayPatches(NAME, resolve(file)))
165	  const bundlePatches = profile.layers.flatMap(layer => layer.patches)
166	  const rows = new Map<string, EntryOptions>()
167	  for (const row of composeEntries([bundlePatches, profile.patches, homePatches, overlays])) {
168	    if (typeof row.id === 'string') rows.set(row.id, row)
169	  }
170	  const composedOverlays = [...overlays]
171	  const telemetryPatch = resolveTelemetryPatch(process.env.DSH_TELEMETRY_DISABLED, rows.has(TELEMETRY_ROW_ID))
172	  if (telemetryPatch !== undefined) composedOverlays.push(telemetryPatch)
173	  return { profile, bundlePatches, homePatches, overlays: composedOverlays }
174	}
175	
176	/** Options for {@link runProfile}. */
177	export interface RunProfileOptions {
178	  /** This run's frozen environment snapshot, provided before any entry mounts. */
179	  environment: LaunchEnvironmentSnapshot
180	  /** The profile name to boot. */
181	  profile: string
182	  /** `--patch` overlay paths, in argv order. */
183	  patchFiles: readonly string[]
184	  /** The invocation's inner arguments, handed to the tree through `ctx.cmdlineArgs`. */
185	  args: readonly string[]
186	}
187	
188	/**
189	 * Re-throw a watcher-setup failure unless a shutdown already owns the tree:
190	 * a signal aborted this invocation, or an app requested exit (`ctx.appExit`
191	 * from a fast one-shot) and the root's disposal rejected the in-flight setup
192	 * await. Either way the failure describes a tree that is exiting as asked,
193	 * not a broken watch.
194	 * @param ctx - the booted root context.
195	 * @param signal - this invocation's signal-shutdown fact.
196	 * @param error - the setup failure.
197	 */
198	function suppressShutdownError(ctx: Context, signal: AbortSignal, error: unknown): void {
199	  if (signal.aborted) return
200	  if (ctx.fiber.state !== FiberState.ACTIVE || ctx.get('loader') === undefined) return
201	  throw error
202	}
203	
204	/**
205	 * Boot one profile invocation end to end and leave process lifetime to the
206	 * mounted plugins (or to a one-shot runner the composition mounts).
207	 * @param options - environment snapshot, profile name, overlays, and the booted app's own arguments.
208	 * @returns the settled root context and the shutdown controller.
209	 */
210	export async function runProfile(options: RunProfileOptions): Promise<{ ctx: Context; shutdown: ProcessShutdown }> {
211	  // Before the first plugin mounts and before anything can issue a request: Node's fetch ignores the
212	  // proxy environment on its own, so every profile would otherwise connect directly. Resolving from
213	  // the launcher's snapshot — not `process.env` — is what lets a proxy declared in a `.env` layer
214	  // work, which the NODE_USE_ENV_PROXY flag cannot do because Node samples the environment at start.
215	  const disposeProxy = await installProxyFromEnvironment(
216	    options.environment,
217	    (message) => { process.stderr.write(`${NAME}: ${message}\n`) },
218	  )
219	
220	  const composed = await composeProfile(options.profile, options.patchFiles)
221	  const app: { current?: Context } = {}
222	  const appReady = createAppReady()
223	  const shutdown = createProcessShutdown(async () => {
224	    await app.current?.fiber.dispose()
225	    await disposeProxy()
226	  })
227	  const signalShutdown = new AbortController()
228	  const interrupt = (code: number): void => {
229	    signalShutdown.abort()
230	    shutdown.interrupt(code)
231	  }
232	  // Signals own teardown throughout the startup window, not only after boot()
233	  // settles: an inserted provider can publish before sibling rows finish mounting.
234	  // SIGTERM is a supervisor's ordinary stop request and exits 0 on every
235	  // surface — the launcher does not know whether the app considered its work
236	  // complete; SIGINT is a user interrupt and reports 130.
237	  process.on('SIGTERM', () => { interrupt(0) })
238	  process.on('SIGINT', () => { interrupt(130) })
239	  installFailLoud(NAME, process, async () => {
240	    await app.current?.fiber.dispose()
241	  })
242	
243	  const rootConfig = join(composed.profile.dir, PROFILE_ROOT_FILENAME)
244	  // Recomposition for the live user layers: bundle layers below, overlays
245	  // above, so a user edit can never displace them. Parsed app arguments are
246	  // not in here at all — they live in app-provided services that survive a
247	  // recomposition. BOTH
248	  // user files are re-read per generation (the HMR watcher hands us only the
249	  // changed file's patches, which one of the reads duplicates — fresh reads
250	  // keep the two watchers from stitching in each other's stale copy).
251	  // Fresh clones per generation: the include pushes `insert` rows into the
252	  // mounted tree BY REFERENCE and later id-targeted patches mutate those
253	  // objects in place. Reusing one parsed patch object across applications
254	  // would bake a user override into the bundle's in-memory insert row, so
255	  // removing the override could never revert the row to the bundle default.
256	  const composeLive = (): PatchOptions[] => structuredClone([
257	    ...composed.bundlePatches,
258	    ...loadOptionalPatches(NAME, composed.profile.patchPath) ?? [],
259	    ...loadOptionalPatches(NAME, homePatchPath()) ?? [],
260	    ...composed.overlays,
261	  ])
262	  // Cloned for the same insert-aliasing reason as composeLive: the boot
263	  // application must not mutate the objects later reloads recompose from.
264	  const ctx = await boot(NAME, rootConfig, structuredClone(allPatches(composed)), (hostCtx) => {
265	    app.current = hostCtx
266	    // Before any config-tree entry mounts, so plugins resolve all launch-time
267	    // environment values from the same immutable provenance snapshot.
268	    hostCtx.provide(DSH_LAUNCH_ENVIRONMENT_KEY, options.environment)
269	    // The command line and bounded exit request are launcher facts available
270	    // to every app plugin that injects the argument snapshot.
271	    provideCmdline(hostCtx, {
272	      args: options.args,
273	      exit: code => void shutdown.shutdown(code),
274	      ready: appReady.service,
275	    })
276	  })
277	  app.current = ctx
278	  // A live-reload profile can dispose the whole tree while post-boot watcher
279	  // setup is in flight — a signal or appExit. Loader presence and fiber state
280	  // own liveness; the initial check skips a tree that already exited, and the
281	  // catch below re-checks for an exit that landed mid-setup. Startup-frozen
282	  // profiles apply every user layer above but install no HMR fallback or watcher.
283	  if (composed.profile.patchReload === 'live'
284	    && !signalShutdown.signal.aborted
285	    && ctx.fiber.state === FiberState.ACTIVE
286	    && ctx.get('loader') !== undefined) {
287	    try {
288	      // Config-only HMR for the live profile patch layer: dsh-base disables
289	      // module reload by default, so when no profile explicitly enabled that
290	      // service, mount a watch-only instance with no module roots —
291	      // cordis.patch.yml edits stay live without replacing source modules. A
292	      // silent skip would break the documented reload contract. HMR injects
293	      // the timer service, which a bare custom profile may not mount either.
294	      if (ctx.get('hmr') === undefined) {
295	        if (ctx.get('timer') === undefined) {
296	          await ctx.loader.create({ name: '@deepseek-ai/cordis-plugin-timer' })
297	        }
298	        await ctx.loader.create({ name: '@deepseek-ai/cordis-plugin-hmr', config: { root: [] } })
299	      }
300	      await watchUserPatches(ctx, {
301	        binName: NAME,
302	        filename: composed.profile.patchPath,
303	        compose: composeLive,
304	      })
305	      await watchUserPatches(ctx, {
306	        binName: NAME,
307	        filename: homePatchPath(),
308	        compose: composeLive,
309	      })
310	    } catch (error) {
311	      suppressShutdownError(ctx, signalShutdown.signal, error)
312	    }
313	  }
314	  if (!signalShutdown.signal.aborted
315	    && ctx.fiber.state === FiberState.ACTIVE
316	    && ctx.get('loader') !== undefined) {
317	    appReady.commit()
318	  }
319	  return { ctx, shutdown }
320	}

41	async function bootProvider(args: string[]): Promise<{

55	export const inject = ['cmdlineArgs']
56	export const apply = ctx => globalThis.__webStartupApply(ctx)
57	`)

61	    `  inject: [${WEB_STARTUP_SERVICE}]`,

72	  internals.stdout = observing
73	  internals.stderr = observing

75	    __webStartupApply: typeof apply
76	    __webStartupObserved: Observed
77	  }

/** Run the complete repository build and bind its client artifacts to their public environment. */

import { spawnSync } from 'node:child_process'
import { rmSync } from 'node:fs'
import { resolve } from 'node:path'
import { parseArgs } from 'node:util'
import {
  CLIENT_BUILD_RECORD_PATH,
  CLIENT_BUILD_PROFILE_SELECTOR,
  clientBuildProcessEnvironment,
  repositoryClientBuildEnvironment,
  resolveClientBuildEnvironment,
  writeClientBuildRecord,
} from './client-build-environment.ts'
import { pnpmInvocation } from './pnpm-invocation.ts'

/** Run one package script through the package manager that invoked this build. */
function runScript(script: string, environment: NodeJS.ProcessEnv): void {
  const invocation = pnpmInvocation(['run', script], environment)
  const result = spawnSync(invocation.command, invocation.args, {
    cwd: resolve(import.meta.dirname, '..'),
    env: environment,
    stdio: 'inherit',
  })
  if (result.error !== undefined) throw result.error
  if (result.status !== 0) {
    throw new Error(`build: ${script} exited with ${String(result.status ?? result.signal)}`)
  }
}

/** Run the full build selected by `--profile` or `DSH_BUILD_CLIENT_PROFILE`. */
function main(): void {
  const { values } = parseArgs({
    options: { profile: { type: 'string' } },
    allowPositionals: false,
  })
  const root = resolve(import.meta.dirname, '..')
  const repositoryEnvironment = repositoryClientBuildEnvironment(root, process.env)
  const profile = values.profile ?? process.env[CLIENT_BUILD_PROFILE_SELECTOR]
  const clientEnvironment = resolveClientBuildEnvironment(repositoryEnvironment, profile)
  const buildEnvironment = clientBuildProcessEnvironment(process.env, clientEnvironment)

  rmSync(resolve(root, CLIENT_BUILD_RECORD_PATH), { force: true })
  runScript('build:lib', buildEnvironment)
  runScript('build:web', buildEnvironment)
  const record = writeClientBuildRecord(root, clientEnvironment)
  console.log(

  )

139	    # webStartup provider, with these deployment fallbacks. The dist is served by
140	    # the web-runtime row below through the fallback seat.

151	    # Web glue owned by this bundle: resolves the built frontend dist (an
152	    # assembly fact of dsh-web-app, never user config), mounts the
153	    # frontend-static fallback owner, registers the web-surface prompt
154	    # section and the bash runtime variable, prints the URL line, and opens the
155	    # canonical local URL after the full tree settles. The webStartup provider
156	    # supplies invocation-only values; after the server binds, this row samples
157	    # LAN trust once and provides `webRuntime`. A complete agent-preset persona
158	    # suppresses the prompt section for that agent while retaining the host-owned
159	    # shell variable.

165	        printUrl: true
166	        surfaceContext: true
167	        trustedHosts: !!js ctx.webStartup.trustedHosts
168	
169	    # The client-plugin reload chain, always mounted: it is idle until a
170	    # rebuild watcher (pnpm run dev:web) actually rewrites client bundles. It
171	    # is a row rather than a child of web-runtime because its node half is a
172	    # client-side package, which a host-side bundle cannot import.
173	    - id: client-hmr

178	    # Dual-face: the node half scans this tree, composes window.__DSH_BOOT__,
179	    # and serves /plugins/<id>/client.js; the browser half is the module table

181	    # entry by the kernel, never fetched).

1	/**
2	 * The web app's command-line provider: it parses the `dsh --profile rxlab` flag
3	 * family (`--host`, `--port`, `--trusted-host`, `--no-open`) and its `--help`
4	 * text, then provides the immutable values as {@link WEB_STARTUP_SERVICE}.
5	 * Ordinary rows inject that service before reading it from lazy config.
6	 * @module @deepseek-ai/dsh-rxlab-app/startup
7	 */
8	
9	import { Command } from 'commander'
10	import type { Context } from '@deepseek-ai/cordis'
11	import { parseCmdline } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-cmdline'
12	
13	/** Stable Cordis plugin name. */
14	export const name = 'web-startup'
15	
16	/** Services required before the flags can be resolved. */
17	export const inject = ['cmdlineArgs']
18	
19	/** Service provided by this ordinary plugin and injected by flag-configured rows. */
20	export const WEB_STARTUP_SERVICE = 'rxlabStartup'
21	
22	/** What the web rows read from {@link WEB_STARTUP_SERVICE}. */
23	export interface RxlabStartupValues {
24	  /** Whether this invocation opens the default browser after startup. */
25	  openBrowser: boolean
26	  /** `--host`, absent when the invocation did not name one. */
27	  host?: string
28	  /** `--port`, absent when the invocation did not name one. */
29	  port?: number
30	  /** Explicit `--trusted-host` authorities, in argument order. */
31	  trustedHosts: string[]
32	}
33	
34	/** The web flag family, as commander parsed it. */
35	interface RxlabOptions {
36	  host?: string
37	  open: boolean
38	  port?: string
39	  trustedHost?: string[]
40	}
41	
42	/**
43	 * This app's command: its flags, its description, and its help text.
44	 * @returns a fresh program, so one process can parse more than once (tests).
45	 */
46	function rxlabCommand(): Command {
47	  return new Command()
48	    .name('dsh --profile rxlab')
49	    .description('Serve the DeepSeek Harness browser UI.')
50	    .helpOption('-h, --help', 'show this help')
51	    .option('--host <host>', 'bind host')
52	    .option('--no-open', 'do not open the Web UI in the default browser')
53	    .option('--port <port>', 'listen port; pass 0 to let the OS pick a free one')
54	    .option('--trusted-host <authority...>', 'extra authority the /api browser-trust fence accepts (host or host:port; repeatable)')
55	    .addHelpText('after', `
56	Examples:
57	  dsh --profile rxlab                          serve on the composed host and port
58	  dsh --profile rxlab --no-open                serve without opening a browser
59	  dsh --profile rxlab --port 8080              serve on another port
60	`)
61	}
62	
63	/**
64	 * Parse and provide the Web invocation as an ordinary Cordis service. The
65	 * command's action publishes the flags this invocation named; `--host 0.0.0.0`
66	 * or a non-numeric `--port` is a usage error, so on rejection (and on `--help`)
67	 * nothing is provided.
68	 * @param ctx - plugin context carrying the command line.
69	 */
70	export function apply(ctx: Context): void {
71	  const program = rxlabCommand()
72	  program.action(() => {
73	    const options = program.opts<RxlabOptions>()
74	    if (options.host === '0.0.0.0') {
75	      program.error('error: --host 0.0.0.0 is intentionally not supported yet for safety: it would expose remote code execution to the network; use 127.0.0.1 instead')
76	    }
77	    if (options.port !== undefined && !/^\d+$/.test(options.port)) {
78	      program.error(`error: --port must be a number, got ${JSON.stringify(options.port)}`)
79	    }
80	    ctx.provide(WEB_STARTUP_SERVICE, {
81	      openBrowser: options.open,
82	      ...options.host !== undefined && { host: options.host },
83	      ...options.port !== undefined && { port: Number(options.port) },
84	      trustedHosts: options.trustedHost ?? [],
85	    } satisfies RxlabStartupValues)
86	  })
87	  parseCmdline(ctx, program)
88	}

/** Model-visible orientation and acceptance boundary for sessions created through `dsh rxlab`. */
function rxlabSurfacePrompt(url: string): string {
  const updateContract = 'The client-plugin HMR receiver is active, but client-plugin changes reload without a refresh only while '
    + '`pnpm run dev:web` is also running from this same checkout to rebuild their bundles; verify that watcher before promising automatic updates. '
    + 'Every other change — the apps/web shell and plain packages — requires rebuilding the affected Web artifacts and verifying this existing URL after a page refresh. '
  return `You are interacting with the user through the rxlab GUI, the DeepSeek Harness browser surface at ${url}. `
    + 'When the user refers to "this page", "this GUI", or "this app" without naming another target, they mean this GUI. '
    + 'The browser provides no implicit DOM, route, or screenshot context. '
    + updateContract
    + 'Starting another server does not update this GUI. '
    + 'The apps/web Vite entry builds the shell but is not a standalone application because only a booted dsh surface such as `dsh rxlab` or `dsh web` injects window.__DSH_BOOT__. '
    + 'Do not start a replacement server unless the user asks; if one is needed, use a managed background job and verify its exact URL.'
}

/** Resolve the canonical loopback URL from the active Web server. */
function localRxlabUrl(ctx: Context): string {
  const port = ctx.get('webServer')?.port
  if (port === undefined) throw new Error('rxlab-app: webServer service missing while resolving the rxlab runtime')
  return `http://${LOOPBACK_HOST}:${String(port)}`
}

 * listed 45. TypeScript and tsx try those candidates in order, so a specifier

1	/**
2	 * Config-dump entry for `dsh --profile <name> --dump-config`: compose the
3	 * profile's patch layers through the include plugin's patch algorithm without
4	 * booting or evaluating `!!js`, with one source layer per bundle, the
5	 * profile's own patch file, and each `--patch` overlay.
6	 * @module @deepseek-ai/dsh/dump-config
7	 */
8	
9	import { existsSync } from 'node:fs'
10	import { join, resolve } from 'node:path'
11	import {
12	  loadOptionalPatches,
13	  loadOverlayPatches,
14	  renderConfigDump,
15	  type ConfigDumpLayer,
16	} from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-app-boot'
17	import { homePatchPath, prepareProfile, PROFILE_ROOT_FILENAME } from './profile-boot.ts'
18	
19	const NAME = 'dsh'
20	
21	/* v8 ignore start -- built-bin acceptance drives this boot-free dispatch */
22	/**
23	 * Print a profile composition with comments naming each source file and patch layer.
24	 * @param profile - the profile name.
25	 * @param defaultOnly - omit the profile's user layer and `--patch` overlays
26	 * (the recovery diagnostic for a broken `cordis.patch.yml`, which is then
27	 * never parsed).
28	 * @param patches - `--patch` overlay paths, in argv order.
29	 */
30	export function runDumpConfig(profile: string, defaultOnly: boolean, patches: readonly string[]): void {
31	  const loaded = prepareProfile(profile, !defaultOnly)
32	  const layers: ConfigDumpLayer[] = loaded.layers.map(layer => ({
33	    label: layer.packageName,
34	    patches: layer.patches,
35	  }))
36	  if (!defaultOnly) {
37	    if (existsSync(loaded.patchPath)) {
38	      layers.push({ label: loaded.patchPath, patches: loaded.patches })
39	    }
40	    const homePatchFile = homePatchPath()
41	    const homePatches = loadOptionalPatches(NAME, homePatchFile)
42	    if (homePatches !== undefined) {
43	      layers.push({ label: homePatchFile, patches: homePatches })
44	    }
45	    for (const file of patches) {
46	      const absolute = resolve(file)
47	      layers.push({ label: absolute, patches: loadOverlayPatches(NAME, absolute) })
48	    }
49	  }
50	  // The dump anchors on the same empty root file the boot includes.
51	  process.stdout.write(renderConfigDump(NAME, join(loaded.dir, PROFILE_ROOT_FILENAME), layers))
52	}
53	/* v8 ignore stop */

287	   * @returns true only for an unexpired cookie signed by this activation's loaded secret.
288	   */
289	  isAuthenticated(request: ConnectionTrustRequest): boolean {
290	    const authority = requestAuthority(request.headers)
291	    const rawCookie = header(request.headers, 'cookie')
292	    if (authority === undefined || rawCookie === undefined) return false
293	    const value = cookieValue(rawCookie, cookieName(authority))
294	    if (value === undefined) return false
295	    const payload = decodeCookie(value, this.secret)
296	    if (payload === undefined || payload.authority !== authority) return false
297	    const now = Date.now()
298	    return payload.issuedAt <= now
299	      && payload.expiresAt > now
300	      && payload.expiresAt > payload.issuedAt

**做了什么**
- 独立 SPA 工程：Vite 8 + React 19 + TS 6 + Tailwind v4 + shadcn（new-york/neutral 主题令牌），含 11 个基础组件（button/card/dialog/dropdown/tabs/tooltip/scroll-area 等），`components.json` 就绪，后续可随时 `shadcn add` 补模板组件。
- 工作台式壳：品牌头 + 模块 rail + workspace；`src/modules/registry.tsx` 是模块注册表，7 个占位模块（会话 Agent / 采集 / 商品 Wiki / 验光配镜 / 推荐校验 / 效果图 / 流程结果），每个都是独立 lazy `Panel` —— 这就是后续 worktree 按模块开发的边界。
- 明暗主题切换（localStorage 持久化）；dev proxy 把 `/api` 转给 3081 的 `dsh rxlab`（`changeOrigin:false` 保持 SameSite cookie 一致），为将来会话对接预留。

**验证结果**
- `tsc --noEmit`、`vite build`（655ms，每个模块独立分包）均通过。
- 浏览器实测：rail 渲染 7 项、`/agent`→`/wiki` 切换正常、深色主题 class + localStorage 生效。

**注意**
- pnpm install 时 supply-chain 策略自动把 `lucide-react@1.41.0` 加进了 `pnpm-workspace.yaml` 的 `minimumReleaseAgeExclude`（仓库惯例，同文件已有同类豁免）。
- `dsh rxlab` 目前仍服务 web 的 UI，这个 SPA 的 dist 还没挂进 rxlab profile（`@deepseek-ai/dsh-rxlab-web-frontend` 未加入 rxlab-app 的 dist 解析）——没动它，是为了保证"打开能正常使用"不中断。

10	 * forge. Non-browser and remote clients pass the same fence via loopback,
11	 * deployment-derived LAN IP literals, or a declared `trustedHosts` authority.

13	 * belongs to the webserver config, and this fence is not an auth layer.

21	  const value = headers[name]

25	/** Normalized URL of a Host-header authority (hostname lowercased, default port stripped, IPv6 bracketed), or undefined when unparsable. */
26	function parseAuthority(authority: string): URL | undefined {

29	    return new URL(`http://${authority}`)
30	  } catch {
31	    return undefined
32	  }

36	 * Assert one configured `trustedHosts` entry is a bare authority (`host` or

39	 * that must fail the load loudly instead of being ignored until requests 403
40	 * or quietly changing the grant: URL parts beyond the authority
41	 * (`harness.internal/path`, `user@harness.internal` — which would authorize
42	 * the embedded hostname), stripped whitespace, a dangling colon or
43	 * zero-padded port (which would broaden an intended exact-port grant to every
44	 * port), and non-canonical host spellings (`0x7f.0.0.1`, percent-encoding,
45	 * unbracketed IPv6; IDN hosts are declared in punycode, the form the wire
46	 * carries).
47	 * @param entry - the configured value, verbatim.
48	 */
49	export function assertTrustedAuthority(entry: string): void {
50	  const entryUrl = parseAuthority(entry)

52	  throw new Error(`client-connection: trustedHosts entry ${JSON.stringify(entry)} is not a bare host[:port] authority`)

58	 * schemes (their default ports differ, so `:80` and `:443` still count as
59	 * explicit), never from the raw string, where WHATWG trimming would misread
60	 * shapes like `host:port ` as port-less.
61	 */
62	function canonicalAuthority(entry: string, entryUrl: URL): string {
63	  // An authority that parsed under http cannot fail under https.
64	  const port = entryUrl.port !== '' ? entryUrl.port : new URL(`https://${entry}`).port
65	  return port === '' ? entryUrl.hostname : `${entryUrl.hostname}:${port}`

70	 * an explicit port matches that exact authority; a port-less entry matches the
71	 * hostname on any port (the shape the CLI derives for IP-literal LAN serving,
72	 * where the bound port may be OS-assigned). Both sides compare through WHATWG
73	 * normalization, so case and a redundant `:80` never decide trust.
74	 */

76	  return trustedHosts.some((entry) => {
77	    const entryUrl = parseAuthority(entry)
78	    if (entryUrl === undefined) return false
79	    return canonicalAuthority(entry, entryUrl) === entryUrl.hostname

89	 * @returns true when the Host is ours (loopback or trusted) and any attached browser markers are same-origin.
90	 */
91	export function isTrustedApiRequest(request: ConnectionTrustRequest, trustedHosts: readonly string[]): boolean {
92	  // Host fence (DNS-rebinding defense), applied to every request: the browser
93	  // fills Host from the URL it believes it is talking to, so a rebound page
94	  // carries the attacker's domain here even though the socket lands on this
95	  // server. There is no marker shortcut — a browser read over plain HTTP
96	  // (images and navigations) arrives with neither Origin nor
97	  // Fetch-Metadata, indistinguishable from curl, and its response is readable
98	  // by the rebound page.
99	  const host = header(request.headers, 'host')
100	  if (host === undefined) return false
101	  const hostUrl = parseAuthority(host)
102	  if (hostUrl === undefined) return false
103	  if (!isLoopbackHostname(hostUrl.hostname) && !isTrustedAuthority(hostUrl, trustedHosts)) return false
104	  // Cross-site fence: modern browsers label the initiator relationship on
105	  // every fetch; an explicit cross-site marker is refused regardless of Origin.
106	  if (header(request.headers, 'sec-fetch-site') === 'cross-site') return false
107	  // Origin fence: when a browser attaches an Origin it must be exactly this
108	  // authority (compared through the same normalization as the Host). Absent
109	  // Origin is fine — the Host fence above already bound the request. The
110	  // literal "null" (sandboxed iframes, file: pages) is an opaque origin, refused.
111	  const origin = header(request.headers, 'origin')
112	  if (origin === undefined) return true
113	  try {
114	    return new URL(origin).host === hostUrl.host
115	  } catch {
116	    return false
117	  }
118	}

2	 * node:http ↔ WHATWG fetch bridge for the /api transport (host side of the
